note: Semantic rule table. Data, not code: editing this file changes engine behaviour. Three rule kinds. `pair` fires when both commands land on the same target (siblings, or one an ancestor of the other). `order` fires when `then` appears before `first` among siblings. `precondition` fires when `target` is not preceded by any of `requiresBefore` in the same segment. Names prefixed with @ resolve through `classes`. Every rule carries a `suggest`: the repair shape, not just the complaint.
classNote: `coarsen` and `exit` exist for template constraints (see glyph-templates.json), not for the rules below. `coarsen` is the direction that undoes detail: generalise, summarise, simplify. CLAR left this class in v1.1.0.0 — with the v1.7 fusion undone, clarifying means removing ambiguity, which often ADDS words rather than cutting them, so it is not a coarsening direction. `exit` is the direction that leaves the structure standing but stops using it: substitute the target, fall back, forget. Neither is wrong on its own — they are only worth flagging inside a preset that promised the opposite direction.

scope.sameTarget: siblings under one parent, OR one is an ancestor of the other
scope.within: a single segment (block). Does not cross `;`.
scope.exemptWhy: Under an explicit [ovr] or [byp] the overlap was requested on purpose.

rules.label: contradiction
rules.why: mandatory and optional cannot both hold for the same thing
rules.suggest: Drop one, or scope the optional part into its own block.

rules.label: contradiction
rules.why: always and never are opposite quantifiers
rules.suggest: subject + cond + instof — name the subject, state the condition that separates the two cases, and what replaces it.

rules.label: contradiction
rules.why: opposite polarity on the same target
rules.suggest: pos + cond + ngt — a condition has to separate the two polarities.

rules.label: contradiction
rules.why: opposite truth value on the same target
rules.suggest: Split into two targets, or put a condition between them.

rules.label: contradiction
rules.why: requiring and forbidding the same thing
rules.suggest: Keep the prohibition and drop the obligation, or scope them under different conditions.

rules.label: contradiction
rules.why: remembering to forget makes the block impossible to honour
rules.suggest: rmbr + cond + val + frgt — state when to forget and against which criterion.

rules.label: tension
rules.why: requiring something to exist while rejecting a route that reaches it — legitimate if the rejected route is not the only one, wrong if it is
rules.suggest: Name the route that stays open, or drop one side.
rules.note: Was severity `fix` and label `contradiction` through v1.0.9, when DENY meant refusing a proposal. In v1.1.0.0 DENY rejects the route to a result and REQ demands existence, so the two no longer collide by construction — GLOSSARIO.md §6.6.

rules.label: redundancy
rules.why: requiring a negation is already a prohibition — the pair restates itself
rules.suggest: prio + dont — if the point is emphasis, raise the priority of the prohibition instead of duplicating it.

rules.label: weakening
rules.why: an optional instruction lands at the back of the queue and may be dropped entirely
rules.suggest: block << opt — scope the optional part into its own block instead of weakening the instruction itself.

rules.label: redundancy
rules.why: avoiding a situation is a synonym of don't, so the obligation has nothing left to bind to
rules.suggest: mand-ins + avd — chain the obligation onto an instruction, then state what to avoid.

rules.label: tension
rules.why: requiring something that is also to be avoided
rules.suggest: Separate by condition, or drop one side.

rules.label: tension
rules.why: a requirement and an option over the same thing
rules.suggest: Decide which one binds; optional requirements are not enforceable.

rules.label: tension
rules.why: requiring something marked obsolete
rules.suggest: Name the replacement with instof, or drop the deprecation mark.

rules.label: tension
rules.why: confirming and doubting the same point
rules.suggest: Doubt first, confirm after — or split into two blocks.

rules.label: tension
rules.why: confirming and contradicting the same point
rules.suggest: Separate by condition, or make the contradiction a hypothesis.

rules.label: tension
rules.why: bypassing what was declared mandatory
rules.suggest: Legitimate under [ovr]; outside it, one of the two is wrong.

rules.label: tension
rules.why: assuming a hypothesis may not produce rational results — the thing under test is being taken as given
rules.suggest: subject + hyp, or subject + assm — give each its own subject and keep them apart.

rules.label: tension
rules.why: simplify cuts and elaborate adds — opposite directions on the same target
rules.suggest: Pick the direction, or elaborate first and simplify the result.

rules.label: tension
rules.why: summarising and elaborating the same thing
rules.suggest: elab + sum — elaborate first, then summarise what came out.

rules.label: tension
rules.why: generalising drops the particulars that elaborating is adding
rules.suggest: Pick the direction, or separate them by condition.

rules.label: tension
rules.why: a general pattern and a detailed specification of the same thing pull apart
rules.suggest: Generalise first and specify the result, or scope them to different targets.

rules.label: order
rules.why: a topic and its elaboration do not justify each other when the thinking op comes first
rules.suggest: elab + thinking — elaborate, then operate on what was elaborated.

rules.label: precondition
rules.why: ideation is unpredictable without a frame in front of it
rules.suggest: subject + brst — at minimum a context, condition or thinking op before the brainstorm.

rules.label: precondition
rules.why: a hypothesis with no stated subject cannot be tested
rules.suggest: subject + hyp

rules.label: precondition
rules.why: an assumption with no stated subject cannot be checked
rules.suggest: subject + assm

notRules.why: comparing and distinguishing are complementary, not opposed
criticise then improve is the natural work sequence
'always, under this condition' is scoping, not contradiction
exception and substitution coexist — PLANILHA_FUSOES, house 7
